Observations & Recommendations

Key Observations

  • Japan region dominates usage — GSSP-JPN and NAT-Banca-JPN alone account for 25% of all executions and 28% of total VUs.
  • CI/API adoption low — Only 3.3% of tests are triggered via API/CI pipeline, indicating significant opportunity to shift-left and automate test triggering in delivery pipelines.
  • Q1 2026 dip — Activity dropped ~45% from the Oct 2025 peak in Jan–Feb 2026, recovering strongly in March, suggesting seasonal project cycles.
  • High average duration — Average test run exceeds 7 hours, reflecting a heavy emphasis on endurance and soak testing across teams.
  • Scale validated — Peak load of 10,000 concurrent virtual users demonstrates platform capability for large-scale enterprise performance validation.

Recommendations

  • Increase CI/CD integration — Grow API-triggered test runs from 3.3% to 20%+ by embedding BlazeMeter into Jenkins / GitHub Actions pipelines.
  • Optimise Training_Workspace — 191 executions in a training workspace suggest teams are running production-scale tests in non-production environments; review and migrate to dedicated project workspaces.
  • Standardise test naming — Multiple runs with "Untitled test" entries make traceability difficult; enforce naming conventions via CI gate checks.
  • Review endurance test scheduling — Concentrate 24-hour endurance tests during off-peak windows to optimise concurrency credit consumption.
